content:
Maya: Quick FYI  planning a minimal-rootfs pivot for worker images next week to reduce runtime attack surface. Need alignment on RBAC for signing, audit logging for attestations, and an emergency key-compromise playbook. Thoughts?
Jordan: +1. Main questions: who can sign artifacts, where do we keep attestations, and how do we detect a tamper after push?
Priya: My proposal: a dedicated signer SA `image-signer-canary@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` with narrowly scoped KMS permissions and no long-lived admin roles. Signing happens via a controller in a small CI runner, not human keys.
Lin: Agree on separation. Two-principal model: (1) signing-controller SA with `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` (or more-restrictive sign role) bound to the signing key, (2) ephemeral deployer SA that can call the controller via `iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` for short-lived ops. Keep the token-creator off the signing principal.
Maya: Good. For attestations, use cosign transparency-style signatures stored alongside artifacts in Artifact Registry and also push a copy to an encrypted GCS bucket `gs://redwood-attest-canary` with restricted ACLs.
Jordan: On detection: run a vulnerability scan job in the canary pipeline that publishes a metric `image_vuln_max_cvss` and fail if >7.0. Also verify cosign signatures as a post-deploy check on each node. If signature verify fails on >1 node, trigger rollback.
Priya: Audit logging: request retention ramp to 72h for canary flows and add a structured label `canary=rootfs-pivot-2026`. Example logging filter for dashboards: `resource.type=\"k8s_container\" AND labels.canary=\"rootfs-pivot-2026\" AND protoPayload.methodName:(\"WriteObject\" OR \"SetAttestation\")`.
Lin: Add an alert: `canary.cosign.failures` if >3 verify failures per node in 15m. Also instrument `canary.vuln.scan.failed` and auto-fail the rollout if threshold exceeded.
sec-oncall: Incident playbook proposal (short): 1) Pause all canaries and pause signing controller. 2) Revoke affected KMS key (create new key in a separate keyring), 3) Re-sign artifacts with emergency key under strict ACLs, 4) Rotate signer SA creds and run an integrity sweep against prod images. I'll draft an expanded runbook.
Maya: Nice. Can we have a lightweight preflight checklist in PR: KMS test sign, cosign verify dry-run, vulnerability scan pass, logging export path exists, alert hooks wired?
Jordan: +1. Also add a preflight to validate IAM bindings with a dry-run script: `gcloud iam roles describe ...` and a simulate-token flow for the ephemeral SA.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled by Maya for Tue 2026-09-07T22:00:00Z (rootfs pivot canary batch 1). Link: https://deployments.redwood.internal/3344556677
Priya: I'll submit the IAM PR tonight with minimal policy and explicit principals, include steps to rotate the canary signer after batch #3 and to revoke tokens.
Maya: I'll update the canary playbook with: ephemeral SA lifecycle, signing-controller config, cosign verification step on nodes, vuln gating, audit export + dashboard, and the incident runbook pointer.
Lin: I'll add the alert rules and the Grafana dashboard panels for `canary=*` logs/metrics.
sec-oncall: I'll join the Tuesday window and runbook review. If anything looks off during PR review, ping oncall.
Maya: Thanks all. Checklist for PR description: 1) IAM policy + SA names 2) KMS key location + keyring segmentation 3) Audit export & retention 72h + query samples 4) Canary gating metrics & alerts 5) Incident key-compromise steps + contact list.
Jordan: If no blockers by EOD I'll approve. Can we also schedule a 20m pre-canary war room 30m before start?
Maya: Yep, scheduling invite now: https://calendar.company/meet/warroom3344. Will post final PR link here once open. :rocket:
